The paradox

Average all the world’s land together and precipitation barely moves.

−1.3% per decade
Land-average trend 2000–2025: −0.88 mm/month per decade, 95% CI [−1.88, 0.12], p = 0.08. The interval includes zero: no detectable global trend.

How NASA data makes it possible

Four NASA products: one to find trends, three to try to break them.

Main record
GLDAS-2.1 Noah
GLDAS_NOAH025_M v2.1 · doi:10.5067/SXAVCZFAQLNO

Monthly precipitation (GPCP-based forcing) on one 0.25° grid, 2000–2025: the trend tests run here.

Independent cross-check
NASA FLDAS Noah
FLDAS_NOAH01_C_GL_M v001 · doi:10.5067/5NHC22T9375G

CHIRPS precipitation (2003–2024): trend signs match on 87% of land where either is significant, 94% where both. Consistently forced soil water (MERRA-2 + CHIRPS forcing).

Control
GLDAS-2.0 Noah
GLDAS_NOAH025_M v2.0 · same model, other forcing

2000–2014: the 2010-08 solar-radiation step shows up only in GLDAS-2.1 (+8.8 vs −1.1 W/m²).

Observations
GRACE / GRACE-FO
JPL GRACE and GRACE-FO MASCON RL06.3Mv04 CRI

Satellite gravity, 2003–2024: 40% of land shows FDR-significant storage trends. NW India: GRACE −204 vs land model +34 mm/decade (groundwater is not in the model).

Ingest
Streaming pipeline

Reads one month at a time and aggregates to 17,284 land tiles of 1°. Quality checks passed.

→
Test
Calibrated trend tests

OLS trend; p is the larger of an AR(1)-corrected and an annual-means test (calibrated to 3–6% false positives), then Benjamini–Hochberg FDR.

→
Map
Spatial clusters

Local Moran’s I with permutation tests finds coherent drying and wetting regions, not lone pixels.

→
Explain
Discovery Cards

8 cards, each graded against the cross-checks above, with a named user, a decision and caveats.

A gap-free, globally consistent NASA record lets a trend in Chile and one in Siberia be measured the same way; independent NASA products let each trend be challenged. Results are “detectable trends”, never causes.

Data: NASA GES DISC (GLDAS, FLDAS) · NASA JPL (GRACE/GRACE-FO mascons) · Rainf_f_tavg4 / 7
A Discovery Card

Every finding arrives with its own evidence grade, and a person who needs it.

wetting · robust pattern: passes all 4 extra checks (windows, neighbours, independent data, literature)
Central Sahel (Chad and eastern Niger)

48 contiguous 1° land tiles, 566,664 km², show a detectable wetting trend over 2000–2025 (median +3.5 mm/month per decade). Statistical trend, not a cause.

+48.5%median per decade
481° tiles
100%tiles FDR-significant
Who decides with this

An agricultural extension office in the central Sahel (e.g. a district extension team in Chad). Decision: Which millet and sorghum varieties and sowing windows to recommend to smallholders for the coming rainy season.

Robustness checklist
  • ✓FDR-corrected significance48 of 48 tiles significant, BH q < 0.05
  • ✓Stability across time windows2000–2025: +48.4% · 2003–2025: +50.0% · 2000–2020: +37.5%
  • ✓Agreement between neighbour definitions (queen vs kNN LISA)100% of queen-LISA HH tiles keep the label under kNN weights
  • ✓Agreement with an independent precipitation product (CHIRPS, via NASA FLDAS)CHIRPS 2003–2024: wetting in 100% of 48 tiles · median +1.0 vs +3.6 mm/month per decade in GLDAS
  • ✓Agreement with independent literature1 agree, 0 partly · Biasutti 2019
4 of 4 checks passed (plus FDR selection)

The detective that checks itself

Paradox Earth caught a false trend: it lines up with changes in the model’s input data.

Incoming solar radiation steps up only in GLDAS-2.1's forcing at 2010-08, and evaporation responds only in 2.1. The 2011-2013 soil-water dip appears in both versions, deeper in 2.1: the forcing change exaggerated a real dip into an apparent long-term decline.

RETRACTED
Soil water 0–200 cm · original headline

A forcing change is not a trend. Our original 26-year soil-water decline was withdrawn instead of published.

In NASA FLDAS, forced consistently with MERRA-2 + CHIRPS over 2003–2024, global land soil water shows no detectable trend: +5.0 mm/decade (95% CI −1.6 to 11.6, p = 0.14).

Who this protects

Teachers and students using the Paradox Earth explorer: Whether to trust a dramatic trend line before checking how the data were made. A tool that rejects its own most exciting result shows why every trend needs a homogeneity check, not just a p-value.

Figure: NASA GLDAS-2.1 vs GLDAS-2.0 (same Noah model, different forcing). The tool rejects its own result when the evidence does not hold.6 / 7
Try it

An explorer anyone can open: click a place, read its case file.

  • Every land tile with its corrected significance, and a graded Discovery Card for each coherent cluster.
  • Forecast lab: a physics-informed CNN emulator of the GLDAS-2.1 land water store beats a linear AR baseline by +0.19 to +0.22 MSESS on a region held out of training; a water-budget penalty (λ = 1) cuts its budget residual from 7.5 to 4.2 mm/month. Emulation skill against a model, not a forecast of reality.
  • Next: more NASA variables, GPM IMERG as a further check, and a card for your own region.
